s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent, severe, unilateral headaches with visual aura and refractory to multiple treatments
salient_findings: Unilateral headache with radiation to multiple regions
Refractory to multiple treatments, including triptans and corticosteroids
key_facts: 17-year history of migraine headaches
Right-sided migraine with visual aura
Pain behind the right eye radiating to the right frontal, temporal, and suboccipital regions
3 to 4 severe migraines per month lasting 3 to 7 days
Relief only from sumatriptan
Failed trials of acetaminophen, ibuprofen, rizatriptan, methylprednisolone, prednisone, and dexamethasone
Developed a new headache pattern in January 2023
Failed treatment with ketorolac, rizatriptan, and dexamethasone taper
Failed treatment with naratriptan, prochlorperazine, acetaminophen, ibuprofen, and diphenhydramine
Unremarkable brain magnetic resonance imaging
Underwent an ultrasound-guided right sphenopalatine ganglion block with bupivacaine and dexamethasone

raw.rationale: The patient's headache is characterized by a continuous, unilateral pain with a new headache pattern developing in January 2023, and the pain is localized to one side of the face, which is consistent with Hemicrania Continua. The patient also experienced a lack of response to various treatments, including triptans and corticosteroids, which is also consistent with this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Chronic Migraine
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of migraines, the new headache pattern and continuous, unilateral pain are not typical of chronic migraine.

rejected.label: Cluster Headache
rejected.why: The patient's headache does not occur in clusters or cycles, and the pain is not strictly unilateral and orbital.

rejected.label: Trigeminal Neuralgia
rejected.why: The patient's pain is not limited to the distribution of the trigeminal nerve, and there are no reports of trigger points or sudden, severe shocks of pain.

rejected.label: Medication Overuse Headache
rejected.why: While the patient has tried various medications, there is no indication that the headaches are a result of medication overuse, and the patient has not reported an increase in headache frequency or severity with medication use.
